analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The PR's changed ranges are head 584-589 (benchmark schema 5 adds prefillChunkTokens and maxBatchedTokensPerStep, which record the scheduler geometry handed to the warm-up engine) and head line 1759 (a new env-var table row for DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS). Neither changed range appears in the supplied units 9 (lines 822-1309) and 10 (lines 1310-1671). I reviewed only the surrounding unchanged text and the patch excerpt, which is truncated. The patch is documentation only: it changes no code, no trust-boundary behavior, no auth, attestation or encryption logic, and no keys or ledger.

I checked the patch against the threat model. T-041 (prefix cache), A-016/T-053 (serving authorization), and TB-010 (fan helper) are unaffected. The documented controls are unchanged: the fan helper requires explicit sudo and a signed-provider lease. Logout does not confirm remote revocation. The report command redacts and bounds its upload. Cache storage and KEK behavior are not altered. The new env vars (prefill chunk and step token budget) are scheduler tuning knobs. They are not forwarded to the LaunchAgent in any way the visible docs show. They add only a possible local-operator availability or performance impact, which sits within the operator-controlled provider process in TB-003. No new attack surface appears in the supplied text.

Integration questions: whether the implementation (EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift, prefillGeometry) bounds the new env overrides is outside the supplied evidence. This is a documentation change, so I raise no finding. I cannot verify the source citations in the docs.
